headline: Prime Video has taken global rights to a Turkish film, spun off from the hit series 'Çukur', that its producer says was generated frame by frame with AI.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a notable step for AI in film, with a major streamer and an established franchise, but the AI claims are the producer's own and there is no release date or audience data.
importance_line: Viewers on a major streaming service get a film from a series the producer says has aired in 105 countries, made with AI-generated visuals, which tests whether audiences and the screen industry accept it, but the production claims come from the producer's own statement and no release date or viewer reaction is reported.
summary: Variety reports, citing a statement from Turkish producer Ay Yapim, that Amazon's Prime Video has taken global rights to 'Çukur: Vartolu', a spin-off film in the world of the long-running drama 'Çukur' (known abroad as 'The Pit') made by Ay Yapim's Singapore-based AI studio, AI Yapim, which says 'every frame' was generated with AI while human actors performed the scenes and human voice actors recorded the dialogue. It follows 'Castle Walls', a two-episode AI-made historical drama from the same studio that reached Prime Video in August, and Variety notes it will be interesting to see how fans of the live-action series react.
notes: Read from the pre-fetched full text of Variety. Claims about AI production come from the Ay Yapim statement. No release date given. 'Amazon's' is general knowledge, not in the article.
